qualification_this_checkpoint.proof_argument: For nonzero integer n, the representation defines theta=atan(1/n) in (-pi/2,pi/2), so its exact argument is the signed rational 1/n. Native Rational inversion preserves that value and rejects zero. Existing consumers use this same principal-branch argument. Independently, tan(theta)=1/n and sin^2+cos^2=1 imply sin^2=1/(n^2+1), cos^2=n^2/(n^2+1), cos>0 and sign(sin)=sign(n). Pi shifts and half-pi complements follow the ordinary trigonometric identities. For s in {-1,+1}, sin(s*pi/2-atan(a))=s/sqrt(1+a^2) and cos(s*pi/2-atan(a))=s*a/sqrt(1+a^2); native composition swaps the same pair and applies s. The family metadata enables existing proof search; it is not itself a new value or sign certificate. This is a local mathematical argument, not formal verification of every consumer.
